objectives.label: Present forms in narration
objectives.description: Recognize present-indicative forms and decide what they mean in their clause, including the older temporal use of haber in ha mucho tiempo. Assessment is limited to explicit present forms and this opening construction.

objectives.label: Imperfect for background and habit
objectives.description: Interpret an imperfect verb as an ongoing background state or a repeated past habit when context supports that reading. Assessment does not cover every contrast between the imperfect and preterite.

objectives.label: Scope of no
objectives.description: Identify the verb or expression negated by no in short clauses and distinguish no quiero from the historical time expression no ha mucho tiempo.

objectives.label: Articles and noun-phrase agreement
objectives.description: Match an article or descriptive adjective to its noun by gender and number in a simple noun phrase. Assessment excludes verb agreement and agreement across long-distance ellipsis.

objectives.label: Acordarse de
objectives.description: Use and interpret acordarse de as a pronominal verb meaning to remember, including an attached pronoun on an infinitive such as acordarme.

objectives.label: Possessive relative cuyo
objectives.description: Connect cuyo, cuya, cuyos, or cuyas to an antecedent while making the form agree with the possessed noun. Assessment uses explicit relative clauses with a clear antecedent.

objectives.label: Quantity and comparison between nouns
objectives.description: Interpret basic quantities, part-to-whole expressions, and comparisons such as más vaca que carnero where the compared terms are nouns.

objectives.label: Weekdays as recurring time
objectives.description: Interpret a plural weekday with the definite article, such as los sábados, as a recurring habit rather than one dated event.

objectives.label: Pronominal se with the subject
objectives.description: Interpret se when a named subject performs an action involving or presenting that same subject, as in se honraba or se viste. Assessment excludes passive and impersonal se.

objectives.label: Historical vocabulary from context
objectives.description: Use a supplied contextual gloss to distinguish people, objects, foods, garments, fabrics, and older forms in the novel's opening. Recall is limited to the explicitly taught opening words.

placement.prompt: Choose the form that completes the current fact: Ahora Lucía ___ en Toledo.
placement.explanation: Vive is present indicative and states where Lucía lives now.

placement.prompt: In an older narrative, what does No ha mucho tiempo most nearly mean?
placement.explanation: Here ha is an older impersonal use of haber in a time expression; the whole phrase means not long ago.

placement.prompt: What does De niño, Tomás leía cada noche tell us?
choices: Reading was Tomás's repeated childhood habit
placement.explanation: Leía is imperfect, and cada noche makes the repeated past habit explicit.

placement.prompt: In Cuando llegué, Ana cocinaba, what was already in progress?
placement.explanation: Cocinaba presents cooking as background activity in progress when the arrival occurred.

placement.prompt: What does No quiero cerrar la puerta mean?
choices: I want to open the door
I do not want to close the door
placement.explanation: No negates quiero: the speaker lacks the desire to close the door.

placement.prompt: Choose the phrase with matching gender and number.
placement.explanation: Espada is feminine singular, so una and antigua match it.

placement.prompt: Complete the noun phrase: ___ libros viejos.
placement.explanation: Libros is masculine plural, so the matching definite article is los.

placement.prompt: Complete the sentence: Quiero ___ de la cita.
placement.explanation: After quiero, the infinitive can carry the pronoun: acordarme de la cita.

placement.prompt: Choose the missing preposition: Carmen no se acuerda ___ la dirección.
placement.explanation: The pronominal verb is acordarse de algo.

placement.prompt: In Conocí a la autora cuyo libro ganó el premio, whose book won?
placement.explanation: Cuyo links libro to the antecedent la autora and agrees with libro.

placement.prompt: Complete the sentence: Visitamos una casa ___ ventanas miran al mar.
placement.explanation: Cuyas agrees with the possessed noun ventanas, which is feminine plural.

placement.prompt: What is being compared in Hay más café que leche?
placement.explanation: Más café que leche compares the quantities of two nouns without repeating a verb.

placement.prompt: What does Los martes estudio con Julia normally express?
choices: A Tuesday in the future only
placement.explanation: The plural weekday with los normally marks a recurring schedule.

placement.prompt: In El viajero se viste antes del amanecer, who gets dressed?
placement.explanation: Se refers back to the named subject el viajero in this pronominal use.

placement.prompt: In the opening of Don Quijote, which gloss best fits hidalgo?
choices: A member of the lower nobility
placement.explanation: Hidalgo names a historical social rank: a man of the lower nobility.

lessons.title: Place, memory, and the opening time frame
lessons.readingGoal: Understand why the narrator withholds the place name and place the hidalgo's life in the past.
lessons.explanation: The opening moves through a relative clause before reaching its main past description. In de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme, cuyo connects nombre to lugar, while acordarme requires de. The phrase no ha mucho tiempo means not long ago in this older use; vivía then supplies the continuing past background.

examples.es: Conocí a un músico cuyo nombre no recuerdo.
examples.en: I met a musician whose name I do not remember.

examples.es: No hace mucho tiempo, vivía cerca del río.
examples.en: Not long ago, I lived near the river.

questions.prompt: Why does the opening not give the place's name?
choices: The narrator says he does not want to remember it
The hidalgo forgot where he lived
questions.explanation: No quiero acordarme says that the narrator does not want to remember the name.

sourceSpan.text: de cuyo nombre no quiero acordarme

questions.prompt: In de cuyo nombre, what does cuyo connect nombre to?
questions.explanation: Cuyo introduces a possessive relation: the name belongs to the previously mentioned lugar.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: In Saludé al vecino cuya hija estudia música, who is the daughter related to?
questions.explanation: Cuya links hija to el vecino and agrees with the feminine singular noun hija.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: Complete Quiero ___ de tu consejo.
questions.explanation: The infinitive keeps the pronominal marker and the complement begins with de: acordarme de.

questions.prompt: What role does vivía play in the opening?
choices: It commands the hidalgo to live
It describes the hidalgo's continuing past situation
questions.explanation: The imperfect vivía establishes the background situation in which the story begins.

lessons.title: Meals, weekly habits, and household means
lessons.readingGoal: Follow the long food list and understand what it says about the hidalgo's recurring expenses.
lessons.explanation: The foods form a long plural subject whose verb, consumían, appears near the end. The imperfect presents a customary expense. Los sábados, los viernes, and los domingos describe a weekly routine. Algo más vaca que carnero compares amounts of foods, and las tres partes de su hacienda is glossed here as three quarters of his income.

examples.es: Los jueves comíamos más sopa que pan.
examples.en: On Thursdays we used to eat more soup than bread.

examples.es: El alquiler consumía gran parte de sus ingresos.
examples.en: The rent used up a large part of their income.

questions.prompt: What does consumían tell us about the listed meals?
choices: They regularly used up much of his income
They were planned for the future
questions.explanation: The imperfect presents this spending as part of the household's customary past routine.

sourceSpan.text: consumían las tres partes de su hacienda

questions.prompt: With the passage gloss supplied, how much of his income did the meals consume?
questions.explanation: The edition's opening annotation interprets las tres partes as three of four parts, or three quarters.

sourceSpan.text: las tres partes de su hacienda

questions.prompt: What do los sábados, los viernes, and los domingos signal?
choices: Three recurring days in a weekly pattern
questions.explanation: Plural weekdays with the definite article describe repeated weekly occasions.

sourceSpan.text: duelos y quebrantos los sábados, lentejas los viernes, algún palomino de añadidura los domingos

questions.prompt: Fresh example: What does Preparaban más arroz que verduras compare?
choices: The amounts of rice and vegetables
questions.explanation: Más arroz que verduras compares quantities of two nouns.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: Which sentence clearly describes a recurring habit?
questions.explanation: Los lunes marks recurring Mondays, and salía presents the repeated past habit.

lessons.title: Clothing, reference, and self-presentation
lessons.readingGoal: Recover who spends the remaining income, what the clothes are, and how the hidalgo presents himself on weekdays.
lessons.explanation: El resto della points back to the hacienda in the previous sentence; della is the older written form de ella. The clothing list is the subject of concluían, which here means used up, while el resto della is placed first as the object. After y, the subject changes back to the hidalgo: se honraba describes how he dressed or presented himself. Several unfamiliar words name garments and wool fabrics, so their contextual glosses carry more meaning than a broad clothing tag.

examples.es: El resto del dinero lo consumían los viajes.
examples.en: Travel used up the rest of the money.

examples.es: Entre semana se vestía con ropa sencilla.
examples.en: On weekdays he dressed in simple clothes.

questions.prompt: What relationship does the first clause describe?
choices: The clothes used up the remainder of his income
The hidalgo sold all his clothes
questions.explanation: Concluían means used up here, and the postposed clothing list is what used up el resto della.

sourceSpan.text: El resto della concluían sayo de velarte, calzas de velludo

questions.prompt: What does della refer back to?
questions.explanation: Della is de ella, and ella resumes hacienda from the previous sentence.

questions.prompt: Who is described by se honraba con su vellorí?
questions.explanation: After the coordinated y, the understood subject returns to the hidalgo; se belongs to that pronominal construction.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: In El actor se vistió antes de salir, who was dressed?
questions.explanation: Se points back to el actor in this reflexive or pronominal use.

questions.prompt: Fresh example: Choose the agreeing phrase.
questions.explanation: Capas is feminine plural, so both las and oscuras agree with it.

questions.prompt: Which group contains fabrics rather than garments?
questions.explanation: Velarte, velludo, and vellorí name fabrics; sayo, calzas, and pantuflos are garments or footwear.

sourceSpan.text: El resto della concluían sayo de velarte, calzas de velludo para las fiestas con sus pantuflos de lo mismo, y los días de entre semana se honraba con su vellorí de lo más fino.
